chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, who said:

I heard him saying, and there had flowed among us a mention of the vagabonds, so Abdullah ibn Aamir said, 'This one narrated to me' – and he gestured towards Ahmad ibn Is'haq that he wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him), asking him about them, so he wrote back to him: 'Kill them'.

key_terms.أَبِي مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, a title for Imam Muhammad ibn Hasan al-Mahdi (peace be upon him).
key_terms.اقْتُلْهُمْ: Kill them, a direct command indicating the ruling for the mentioned group.
key_terms.الصَّعَالِيكِ: Vagabonds or roving bandits, often referring to those who commit highway robbery or spread corruption.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for Saa'alik (vagabonds/bandits) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records a direct command from Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him) to 'kill them' regarding the Saa'alik, a term often interpreted in Shia jurisprudence as roving bandits or those who spread corruption (Muharibun). The brevity of the reply suggests an established legal precedent for their execution, aligning with the Quranic category of those who wage war against God and His Messenger. This ruling underscores the executive authority of the Imam in dealing with specific criminal elements who disrupt social order.
